data.name: Chandrashekar
data.gender_notes: Chandrashekar is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Chandrashekar is a Sanskrit name derived from two words: 'Chandra' meaning Moon and 'Shekar' meaning Lord or God's Power. This name is a reference to the moon god, Soma or Chandra, who is considered the god of the night and the giver of light. The name Chandrashekar carries the meaning “Moon–God's–Power” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Chandrashekar usually hope their child will grow to embody moon–god's–power and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Chandrashekar belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Moon–God's–Power.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Chandrashekar total 3, giving a life-path number of 3. Number 3 is linked with Jupiter and with the qualities of creativity, expression and optimism.

data.cultural_impact: The name Chandrashekar holds significant cultural importance in Indian society, as it pays homage to various Hindu deities and their respective domains. The prefix 'Chandra' represents the ever-changing and transformative nature of the moon, and the suffix 'Shekar' emphasizes the unchanging and omnipotent nature of the divine. This name is also used as a title of respect for scholars, learned individuals, and religious leaders.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Chandrashekar holds immense spiritual significance for Hindus, as it represents the union of the divine energies of the moon god and the supreme consciousness of Lord Shiva (Shekar). It is believed that the power of the moon gives wisdom and intelligence, while the Lord's Shekar represents the ultimate truth and spiritual realization. The name is a constant reminder of the connection between the self and the divine and the importance of maintaining a balanced and enlightened state of being.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Chandrashekar: Moon (Chandra) God (Ishwar/Shekar) in one's heart, symbolizing eternal illumination and divine guidance.

historical_references.reference: Chandrashekar, S. Raman (1916-1974): A renowned Indian mathematician who made significant contributions to various fields of mathematics including number theory, topology, and differential equations. He was awarded the Fields Medal in 1935, the first Indian to receive this prestigious award. In 1952, he moved to the United States to take up a position at the Institute for Advanced Study in Princeton, New Jersey.

Chandrashekar, Tirumular (circa 5th century CE): A Tamil poet, philosopher and saint, commonly known as Thirumular or Thirumoolar. He is believed to have authored the holy text, 'Thirumurai', which is the foremost work of the Tevaram collection of hymns and is considered as one of the fundamental texts of the Tamil Shaivite tradition. Thirumular's poems have profound spiritual messages and are deeply connected to the natural world.

modern_usage.modern_context: The name 'Chandrashekar' is of Hindu origin and translates to 'Moon-sized', 'Moon-like'. In modern times, this name has gained significant recognition in the fields of Technology, Mathematics, and Astronomy. In Technology, there is a well-known algorithm named 'Chandrasekhar-Boltzmann Equation' used for calculating the statistical equilibrium of a plasma. In Mathematics, 'Chandrasekhar limit', a theoretical maximum mass for a stable white dwarf, has been named after the renowned Indian-American astrophysicist, Subrahmanyan Chandrasekhar. In Astronomy, the term 'Chandrashekhar Pulsar' refers to a specific type of neutron star. The name has a global presence and is frequently used in scientific research, academic publications, and professional networking.
